title: C rpl: wire 64-bit DAO origin sequence into rpl_dao_build.c TX path (replace uint8 lollipop)
description: Child of b7z9.11, lands after the TX-state child. rpl_dao_build.c:117,264 uses uint8 RFC6550 lollipop dao_sequence in RAM; wire the 64-bit origin sequence TX state: gate TX on the committed/reserved sequence (crash-safe ordering: sequence+signed bytes persisted before transmission, R-09-009/010), stop origination on missing/corrupt state, no equal-sequence rebuild. Coordinate with the wire format: the DAO base carries the low byte (lollipop-visible) while the full 64-bit sequence rides the DAO Origin Signature option (see dao_origin.rs / DaoOriginSignature wire). Verify with the rpl_dao_sequence host harness extended for reboot/corruption matrices. Discovered from project-LICHEN-worker6-b7z9.11.
close_reason: 64-bit DAO origin sequence wired into the C TX path: lichen_rpl_dao_manager gains an optional durable binding (ops/user/opened-state, require_persisted); when bound, build_dao_mut AND build_dao_copy_with_lifetime reserve the next sequence via lichen_rpl_dao_tx_reserve_next BEFORE the frame is built (persist-before-transmit, R-09-009/010; crash wastes a sequence but never transmits an unpersisted one), the DAO base lollipop byte is the reserved sequence's low byte (no independent increment; RFC 6550 7.1/7.2 comparisons hold across region boundaries), and missing/corrupt/unreservable state stops origination fail-closed with the new LICHEN_RPL_ERR_TX_STATE (-9) — no RAM-lollipop fallback. Unbound managers keep bit-identical prior behavior. Host tests extended in tests/rpl_dao_sequence: unbound lollipop parity, missing-state stop, provision+bind+build low-byte, durable alternation, reboot matrix, corruption matrix (torn slot in place), copy-path binding coverage, NULL bind. Gates: ctest 2/2 green under ASan/UBSan, gcc -Werror -Wconversion clean, cppcheck clean. Reviews: pass1 correctness (kimi-k3) found copy-path bypass, error-taxonomy flattening, stale doc ref, misleading comment — all fixed (incl. copy-path tests); passes 2-3 timed out 3x/3x -> self-review fallback per loop protocol (fail-closed, reuse windows, TOCTOU, monotonicity, buffer bounds verified as summarized). 64-bit origin sequence persistence chain (b7z9.11.1/2/3) is now complete across codec, storage, state machine, and TX wiring; remaining: finalize/ack integration into the production DAO send loop (caller-side, no production caller of dao_manager exists yet).
